references_named: Robert & Ethel Scull collection sale, Sotheby Parke-Bernet, 18 October 1973
rationale: The mechanism is the argument: a range slider that only goes up is the literal enactment of speculative bidding, and crossing the hidden reserve is what removes the work from view. The Scull/Rauschenberg anchor is precise and historically literate, and the $0 line for the artist lands the resale-royalty critique without a wall text. It extends the catalogue's value/authenticity line (Three Ball Total Equilibrium Slot Machine, For the Love of Fame, Art is Money) with a new mechanism — the bid as instrument of disappearance — and the per-visit hidden reserve plus the chance gesture in the painting keep it on the chance/order axis. Voice is dry auctioneer deadpan, license and privacy are stated, and the work is materially distinct from every catalogued entry.
reservations: The painting itself is a thin placeholder (a few coloured rects plus a curve); the conceptual weight lives entirely in the bidding mechanic and the ledger, which is fine but means the visual surface is the weakest part. The reserve range (75k–250k) is a touch arbitrary and could be tightened to make the crossing feel more inevitable.
revision_suggestion: Consider giving the painting a more recognisable 'after Rauschenberg' visual cue (a single off-white field with one gestural mark, say) so the surface gag — that this specific kind of work is what the market removes — reads even faster, and tighten the reserve band so the crossing is more reliably dramatic.
